name: Leopard
group: Animals > Mammals > Wild animals on land > Eats only meat

features.claim: It has a slender, muscular body.
features.quote: Its body is slender and muscular, reaching a length of 92–183 cm (36–72 in) with a 66–102 cm (26–40 in) long tail and a shoulder height of 60–70 cm (24–28 in).

features.claim: Its fur is pale yellowish to dark golden with dark spots grouped in rosettes.
features.quote: It has a pale yellowish to dark golden fur with dark spots grouped in rosettes.
Its underbelly is white and its ringed tail is shorter than its body.

features.claim: Its tail is ringed and shorter than its body.
features.quote: Its underbelly is white and its ringed tail is shorter than its body.

features.claim: Its fur is generally soft and thick, softer on the belly than on the back.
features.quote: The leopard's fur is generally soft and thick, notably softer on the belly than on the back.

features.claim: Its tail has a white tip and is white underneath.
features.quote: Its white-tipped tail is about 60–100 cm (23.6–39.4 in) long, white underneath and with spots that form incomplete bands toward the end of the tail.

features.claim: It has relatively short limbs and a broad head.
features.quote: The leopard is a slender and muscular cat, with relatively short limbs and a broad head.

features.claim: Males are larger and heavier than females.
features.quote: It is sexually dimorphic with males larger and heavier than females.

features.claim: It has whitish spots on the back of its ears.
features.quote: The whitish spots on the back of its ears are thought to play a role in communication.

features.claim: Its spots fade toward the white underbelly and the insides and lower parts of the legs.
features.quote: Spots fade toward the white underbelly and the insides and lower parts of the legs.

features.claim: It has well-camouflaged fur, usually tan, with spots called rosettes and a lighter-coloured underside.
features.quote: They have well-camouflaged fur, which is usually tan, and spots (called rosettes). They usually have a lighter-coloured underside.

second_reading.claim: The sources do not agree on how many subspecies of leopard there are.
second_reading.quote: Today, eight subspecies are recognised in its wide range in Africa and Asia.
second_reading.why: the sentence does not support it

second_reading.claim: The simple source says there are nine subspecies, one in Africa and eight in Asia.
second_reading.quote: There are nine subspecies of leopards recognized today, one in Africa and eight in Asia.

second_reading.claim: It is not well understood why some leopards have a reddish 'strawberry' colour.
second_reading.quote: The cause of this morph known as a "strawberry leopard" or "pink panther" is not well understood.
